intro_html: Balsamic vinegar and a touch of brown sugar cook down into a rich, tangy-sweet glaze that makes plain pork feel special. Served over potatoes with green beans, each bowl brings 57 grams of protein for about $5.13 (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings from one batch means the hard part is already done.
cost_closing_html: About $5.13 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each serving comes in around 556 calories with 57 grams of protein.
upsell_html: A little tang, a little sweet, and a whole lot of easy. That is a keeper. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: A bottle of balsamic vinegar costs a couple bucks and flavors many meals, so the splash here is basically free per serving.
Potatoes and green beans are both cheap, filling sides. Buy the potatoes by the 8 lb bag to get the lowest price per pound.
Frozen or fresh green beans both work. Grab whichever is cheaper that week and do not overthink it.
make_it: Rub the pork tenderloin with a little olive oil and set it in the slow cooker with the potatoes.
Whisk the balsamic vinegar, brown sugar, soy sauce, and chicken broth, then pour it over.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork and potatoes are tender.
Steam the green beans until crisp-tender and set aside.
Shred the pork and stir it back through the balsamic glaze.
Divide the pork, potatoes, and green beans into your containers.
